Questions 27–30

Write the correct letter, A, B or C, next to Questions 27-30.

Types of articles 27

transcript.en: Tom, could I ask you for some advice, please?
transcript.zh: 汤姆,请问我能向你征求一些意见吗?

transcript.en: Yes of course, if you think I can help. What's it about?
transcript.zh: 当然可以了,只要你觉得我能帮得上忙。关于什么的?

transcript.en: It's my first media studies assignment, and I'm not sure how to go about it.
transcript.zh: 是我的第一份关于媒体研究的作业,我不确定要怎么做。

transcript.en: You must have done it last year.
transcript.zh: 你去年一定做过这个。

transcript.en: Is that the one comparing the coverage of a particular story in a range of newspapers?
transcript.zh: 是比较不同报刊中的对特定故事报道的那个吗?

transcript.en: That's right.
transcript.zh: 就是那个。

transcript.en: Oh yes, I really enjoyed writing it.
transcript.zh: 对,我写过。我当时还写得很开心。

transcript.en: So what sort of things do I need to compare?
transcript.zh: 所以我需要比较哪些事情呢?

transcript.en: Well, there are several things.
transcript.zh: 有很多可比的。

transcript.en: For example, there's the question of which page of the newspaper the item appears on.
transcript.zh: 比如,关于报道出现在报纸的哪一版面。

transcript.en: You mean, because there's a big difference between having it on the front page and the bottom of page ten, for instance?
transcript.zh: 你的意思是,比方说,把它放在报纸头版和在第十页的底部是有很大差别的?

transcript.en: Exactly. And that shows how important the editor thinks the story is.
transcript.zh: 你说对了。这显示了编辑认为这个故事有多重要。

transcript.en: Then there's the size - how many column inches the story is given, how many columns it spreads over.
transcript.zh: 然后还可以讨论篇幅。报道的列长是多少,占了几列。

transcript.en: And I suppose that includes the headline.
transcript.zh: 我觉得还应该包括标题。

transcript.en: It certainly does. It's all part of attracting the reader's attention.
transcript.zh: 当然了。就是这部分吸引读者的注意力。

transcript.en: What about graphics - whether there's anything visual in addition to the text?
transcript.zh: 配图呢?文本旁边有没有加上任何可视化信息?

transcript.en: Yes, you need to consider those, too, because they can have a big effect on the reader's understanding of the story - sometimes a bigger effect than the text itself.
transcript.zh: 可以。你也需要考虑那些,因为它们会很大程度上影响读者对报道的理解,有的时候比文章本身的影响还要大。

transcript.en: Then you'll need to look at how the item is put together: what structure is it given?
transcript.zh: 接着,你需要看看整个故事是怎么编排的:报道的结构是什么?

transcript.en: Bear in mind that not many people read beyond the first paragraph, so what has the journalist put at the beginning?
transcript.zh: 你要记住很多人都只读第一段,即记者在文章开头写了什么?

transcript.en: And if, say, there are conflicting opinions about something, does one appear near the end, where people probably won't read it?
transcript.zh: 还有,比如,假设有冲突的观点,如果它出现在报道结尾的话,大家是不是可能不会读到?

transcript.en: And newspapers sometimes give wrong or misleading information, don't they?
transcript.zh: 另外,新闻有时候会呈现错误或者有误导性的消息,对吗?

transcript.en: Either deliberately or by accident. Should I be looking at that , too?
transcript.zh: 不管是故意的还是不小心的。我要不要也说一下这个?

transcript.en: Yes, if you can. Compare what's in different versions, and as far as possible, try and work out what's true and what isn't.
transcript.zh: 如果你能完成,可以。比较不同的版本，尽可能地区分开真实的和错误的信息。

transcript.en: And that relates to a very important point: what's the writer's purpose, or at least the most important one, if they have several.
transcript.zh: 这与一个非常重要的观点相关：作者的目的是什么，或者至少是最重要的目的，如果他们有多个目的。

transcript.en: It may seem to be to inform the public, but often it's that they want to create fear, or controversy, or to make somebody look ridiculous.
transcript.zh: 看起来可能是为了向公众传递信息,但是他们经常想要制造恐慌或争议,或是想要让某些人出丑。

transcript.en: Gosh, I see what you mean.
transcript.zh: 天哪,我懂你的意思。

transcript.en: And I suppose the writer may make assumptions about the reader.
transcript.zh: 我认为作者可能做出关于读者的假设。

transcript.en: That's right - about their knowledge of the subject, their attitudes , and their level of education, which means writing so that the readers understand without feeling patronised.
transcript.zh: 是的,关于他们对这一题材的了解、态度和教育水平。这就意味着作者需要写出让读者理解的文章,而不是居高临下。

transcript.en: All of that will make a difference to how the story is presented.
transcript.zh: 所有这些都会影响报道的呈现。

transcript.en: Does it matter what type of story I write about?
transcript.zh: 我写什么类型的故事重要吗?

transcript.en: No - national or international politics, the arts ... Anything, as long as it's covered in two or three newspapers.
transcript.zh: 不重要,国內国际政治,艺术...什么都行,只要在两三份报纸上报道过就行。

transcript.en: Though of course it'll be easier and more fun if it's something you're interested in and know something about.
transcript.zh: 当然，如果你对某个话题感兴趣并且有所了解，那么写作将会更加轻松愉快。

transcript.en: And on that basis a national news item would be worth analysing - I'm quite keen on politics, so I'll try and find a suitable topic.
transcript.zh: 这么说的话，一个国内的新闻报道应该值得分析。我很关心政治,所以我会尝试找到合适的话题。

transcript.en: What did you choose for your analysis, Tom?
transcript.zh: 汤姆,你是怎么选择你的分析内容的?

transcript.en: I was interested in how newspapers express their opinions explicitly, so I wanted to compare editorials in different papers.
transcript.zh: 所以当时我想比较不同报纸的社论。

transcript.en: But when I started looking, I couldn't find two on the same topic that I felt like analysing.
transcript.zh: 我对报纸如何明确表达观点很感兴趣，但是,在我开始研究的时候,我找不到两篇我想分析的、讲述相同话题的报道。

transcript.en: In that case, I won't even bother to look.
transcript.zh: 那种情况下,我就不会去看了。

transcript.en: So in the end I chose a human interest story - a terribly emotional story about a young girl who was very ill, and lots of other people - mostly strangers - raised money so she could go abroad for treatment.
transcript.zh: 所以最后我选择了人们都感兴趣的话题,是一个特别引发人们情感的故事:一个小女孩生病了,很多人,大多数是陌生人给她捐款筹钱,所以她能够去国外接受治疗。

transcript.en: Actually, I was surprised - some papers just wrote about how wonderful everyone was, but others considered the broader picture, like why treatment wasn't available here.
transcript.zh: 实际上,我特别吃惊。因为一些报纸只说了大家是有多善良,但是其它的报纸从更高的角度考虑,比如讨论为什么在我们国家无法治疗。

transcript.en: Hmm, I usually find stories like that raise quite strong feelings in me! I'll avoid that.
transcript.zh: 嗯,我经常发现这样的故事会让我很激动。我会避开这一类。

transcript.en: Perhaps I'll choose an arts topic, like different reviews of a film, or something about funding for the arts - I'll think about that.
transcript.zh: 也许我会选择艺术,比如一部电影的不同评论。或者关于艺术基金的。我会好好考虑。

transcript.en: Yes, that might be interesting.
transcript.zh: 好的,应该会很有趣的。

transcript.en: OK, well thanks a lot for your help, Tom. It's been really useful.
transcript.zh: 好的,谢谢你的帮助,汤姆。你的建议真的很有用。

transcript.en: You're welcome . Good luck with the assignment, Hazel.
transcript.zh: 客气啦。希望你的作业顺利完成。
